title: Joint Navigation and Manipulation Planning with 3D Interaction Chains
claim: Coupling navigation and manipulation through a shared 3D map, waypoint chains and joint scoring yields plans that serve both skills.
layout: Dense multi-stage flow, left-to-right then bottom row, colored background panels per stage
description: A dense, left-to-right pipeline diagram with pastel-colored stage panels. At top left, RGB and depth images plus camera pose and intrinsics feed a trapezoidal Visual Encoder. The encoder output passes into a pink panel. It shows patch features, projected locations, and an 'update' arrow into a top-down 3D feature map with a checkered heatmap. Below, an orange panel runs left to right: interaction waypoints (x,y,z,θ) on a floor plan, candidate waypoint sets (move, grasp, move, place), a 3D chain sketch with colored nodes, and feature aggregation on the map. At right, a blue column shows two 3D interaction chains (move, pick, move, place). These feed MLLM policy, distance and progress boxes, then Joint Planning picks a chain. The chain is routed to a navigation or manipulation local policy. The eye starts at the top left and follows the arrows.
caption: The framework of 3D-IC. Patch features are extracted from RGB images and projected to establish a 3D feature map. Candidate interaction waypoints are generated on the 3D feature map to construct candidate interaction chains. Subsequently, feature aggregation is performed to obtain Z(wk). In the chain decision stage, joint planning is employed to ultimately select the interaction waypoints for execution, which are then dispatched to the local policy based on the task type.
abstract: Open-vocabulary mobile manipulation (OVMM) requires long-horizon navigation in unseen environments and object-centric manipulation. Most existing methods treat navigation and manipulation as separate stages, which can yield navigation endpoints that are poor for manipulation or manipulation-friendly poses that are globally inefficient. We address this mismatch with 3D Interaction Chains (3D-IC), a unified framework that couples multi-stage navigation and manipulation planning. 3D-IC maintains a shared 3D feature map for both skills, generates stage-aligned interaction waypoints, and links them into candidate multi-stage chains. A hierarchical policy then scores these chains by jointly considering feasibility (via VLM reasoning over waypoint-centric 3D features) and transition cost, selecting the best trade-off between success and path efficiency. The robot executes the next waypoint and replans as new observations arrive. Experiments in simulation and on a real Stretch 3 robot demonstrate consistent gains in both task success and trajectory efficiency.
